title: Houellebecq Saw This Coming
author: Louis Betty
content:
![Houellebecq Saw This
Coming](https://storage.ghost.io/c/65/af/65afbdb5-30bf-4286-acc4-9535069adb42/content/images/2026/11/AP17284636568040.jpg)

Michel Houellebecq's novels are our age's most profound and devastating
studies in what it means to be godless. Pascal wrote that "nothing more surely
underlines an extreme weakness of mind than the failure to understand the
unhappiness of someone without God." Houellebecq's body of work is, in some
sense, simply the working out in fiction of this observation. The godlessness
he depicts is not only personal and social but (as explored in
[__Submission__](https://www.amazon.com/Submission-Novel-Michel-Houellebecq-
ebook/dp/B00VE732VM/?_encoding=UTF8&pd_rd_w=qtmpL&content-
id=amzn1.sym.ac827e48-2948-4721-83ef-3e7648ac35cb&pf_rd_p=ac827e48-2948-4721-83ef-3e7648ac35cb&pf_rd_r=131-3731629-2849128&pd_rd_wg=13ZjB&pd_rd_r=0e9b6af9-86dd-4ab4-9263-37770be7b1e0&th=1&ref=compactmag.com))
political and civilizational as well.

Considerations like these make what is now happening to Houellebecq feel all
the more revealing. The author is
[_accused_](https://www.nytimes.com/2026/11/11/arts/michel-houellebecq-
investigated-anti-muslim-remarks.html?ref=compactmag.com) of making statements
liable to "incite racial and religious hatred," a crime under French law, for
claiming in [_a 2022 interview_](https://www.abebooks.com/Front-populaire-
hors-s%C3%A9rie-Fin-lOccident-Houellebecq/31394417184/bd?ref=compactmag.com)
that native Frenchmen were arming themselves to resist the future Muslim
domination of France. In particular, Houellebecq likened potential nativist
violence to so many "Bataclans in reverse," a reference to the 2015 Islamist
terror attack in Paris that left nearly one hundred people dead. Muslims, he
added, were not likely to respond to attacks against them by lighting candles
and carrying bouquets of flowers.
